data.one_liner: Generates boilerplate for Flutter ThemeExtension classes using annotations.
data.what_it_does: Theme Tailor reads @TailorMixin annotations and creates mixins that implement copyWith, lerp, hashCode, and debugFillProperties for ThemeExtension subclasses. It also supports JSON serialization and custom type encoding.
use_when: You need to create many ThemeExtension classes and want to avoid manual boilerplate.
You want compile‑time safety and IDE support for theme properties.
You prefer a generator that works with build_runner.
avoid_when: You only have a few simple theme extensions and don’t want a code generator.
You cannot add build_runner or other dev dependencies to the project.
strengths: Integrates with build_runner and supports custom encoders
Handles JSON serialization and debug diagnostics automatically
weaknesses: Requires build_runner setup and dev dependencies
Generated code may need manual tweaks for complex cases
data.setup_notes: Add build_runner (dev), theme_tailor (dev), and theme_tailor_annotation (regular) dependencies, create part files, and run flutter pub run build_runner build.
